---
title: Prepare identifiers well
---

## Core identifier fields

Common linkage fields include names, dates of birth, sex, addresses, postcodes, and administrative IDs. Each behaves differently: names vary in spelling, dates transpose easily, and addresses often change over time.

## Standardisation steps

- normalise case and whitespace
- strip punctuation that is not informative
- split compound fields consistently
- encode missingness explicitly rather than silently dropping records
- preserve raw values for audit and reruns

::: {.callout-warning .pitfall}
## Pitfall

If you overwrite raw identifiers during cleaning, you lose the ability to inspect disagreement patterns later.
:::

## Missingness and encoding

Missingness is part of linkage information. A blank date of birth is different from an impossible date, and both are different again from a parse failure caused by encoding.
